chunks: He is Duwaid bin Nahad bin Zaid bin Aswad bin Aslam bin Haaf bin Qaza-a.
Abu Hatim has said with regard to him: He lived for 456 years. His bequests and reports are famous and well known.

And from his saying: The passage of time has rendered my limbs useless, and whatever is improved by this period, another day will corrupt it, because that which it has improved today, tomorrow it would destroy it.

key_terms.أَخْبَارُهُ: His reports or stories, noted as being famous
key_terms.الدَّهْر: Time or age, often personified in Arabic poetry as a force of change
key_terms.دَوِيدُ بْنُ نَهْدٍ: Duwaid ibn Nahad, the subject of the biography
key_terms.وَصِيَّتُهُ: His bequests or will, noted as being well-known

ai.seo_question: Who is Duwaid ibn Nahad and what is his recorded lifespan in Shia historical sources?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi cites Abu Hatim’s tradition to record Duwaid ibn Nahad’s extraordinary lifespan of 456 years, situating him within the broader Shia scholarly discourse on *al-Dahr* (time/destiny) as a force of cyclical change. The entry underscores the cultural significance of his well-known will and poetic reflection on time’s dual nature of creation and destruction, illustrating the pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arab understanding of temporal transience.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: He is Duwaid bin Nahad bin Zaid bin Aswad bin Aslam bin Haaf bin Qaza-a.
Abu Hatim has said with regard to him: He lived for 456 years. His bequests and reports are famous and well known

and a sample of his couplets is as follows: The passage of time has rendered my limbs useless and whatever is improved by this period, another day will corrupt it, because that which it has improved today, tomorrow it would destroy it.
